doc.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021

title: Gratitude on the bandstand with Joe Wilder and others
summary: Playing with elder musicians like Wilder is joyful and teaches being in the moment.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah I was wondering if you had words for — I have this little scenario in my head, you’re playing a gig with Frank Wess in a club in New York and it went well. And on the way home what are you feeling inside after that experience?

I’m — well look I’m relatively critical of my own playing and I’m probably less concerned with how other people performed on a given night you know. Was I in a good zone? Was everything working well? Was my — all my antennas working well? I don’t know. I’m not quite so analytical that I make a whole study of it. Basically the gig is over, on to the next.
I see. I guess what I was wondering about —
I’m not sure what you are getting at.

Well I over the years have been lucky through this project I do to find myself briefly on a bandstand with people like Joe Wilder and of that generation. And I just remember almost like I need to pinch myself. Because here I am and there he is and I was hoping to do a good job but I think I just was filled with gratitude that that could happen, that this was happening.

Yeah. I mean look there’s — just listening – I worked a fair amount with Joe Wilder and just listening to him play is so wonderful, as is with so many of these musicians we’re talking about. There’s great joy and satisfaction of just being on the bandstand regardless of what you do, just listening to what comes out of their horn. And you’ve got a job to do and you do it as well as you can. And this experience of this collaborative art form

teaches you how to be in the moment and in the present. And to me the whole game that ties everything together is the cooperation or the successful cooperation of your conscious and subconscious. You know what I mean by that?
I’d be happy to have you expand on that.
